rulers.title: Roman emperors (to the division of 395)
rulers.note: how = how the reign ended (natural, accident, killed in battle, murdered, executed, suicide, deposed, abdicated, unknown); died/death give later fate where the reign ended otherwise. Overlapping reigns are co-emperorships. 'from' is the year of elevation to Augustus.

list.name: Augustus
list.note: Sole master of the Roman world from Actium (2 Sep 31 BC) and Alexandria (Aug 30 BC); name Augustus voted 16 Jan 27 BC. Died at Nola 19 Aug AD 14 after 40 years 7 months of sole rule.

list.name: Tiberius
list.note: Died at Misenum 16 Mar 37 aged 77. Tacitus, Suetonius and Dio report rumours that the prefect Macro smothered him or Caligula poisoned him.

list.name: Caligula
list.note: Stabbed in a palace passage 24 Jan 41 by the praetorian tribunes Cassius Chaerea and Cornelius Sabinus; wife Milonia Caesonia and infant daughter killed the same day.

list.name: Claudius
list.note: Died 13 Oct 54. Tacitus, Suetonius and Dio say Agrippina had him poisoned (mushrooms, with the poisoner Locusta and doctor Xenophon); a minority of modern scholars allow natural death.

list.name: Nero
list.note: Declared hostis by the Senate; stabbed himself in the throat with the help of the freedman Epaphroditus at Phaon's villa outside Rome, 9 Jun 68. Last of the Julio-Claudians.

list.name: Galba
list.note: Proclaimed by his troops in Hispania Tarraconensis Apr 68, recognized by the Senate Jun 68; cut down in the Forum near the Lacus Curtius 15 Jan 69 by praetorians who had hailed Otho.

list.name: Otho
list.note: Stabbed himself at Brixellum 16 Apr 69, two days after his army's defeat at the first battle of Bedriacum, reportedly to spare further civil war.

list.name: Vitellius
list.note: Proclaimed by the Lower German legions at Colonia 2 Jan 69; dragged through the Forum and killed at the Gemonian Stairs 20 Dec 69 as Flavian troops stormed Rome.

list.name: Vespasian
list.note: Proclaimed at Alexandria 1 Jul 69 (his dies imperii); died of fever and diarrhoea at Aquae Cutiliae 23 Jun 79, joking 'I think I am becoming a god'.

list.name: Titus
list.note: Died of fever 13 Sep 81 at the Flavian villa near Reate after a reign of 26 months marked by Vesuvius (79) and the fire and plague at Rome (80).

list.name: Domitian
list.note: Stabbed 18 Sep 96 by the steward Stephanus in a plot involving the chamberlain Parthenius and probably Domitia and both praetorian prefects; damnatio memoriae followed.

list.name: Nerva
list.note: Senatorial choice on Domitian's death; humiliated by the praetorian mutiny of Casperius Aelianus (97), he adopted Trajan in Oct 97; died 27 Jan 98 of a fever.

list.name: Trajan
list.note: First emperor born in a province (Italica, Baetica). Died at Selinus in Cilicia c. 8 Aug 117 after a stroke on the way home from Mesopotamia; Hadrian's adoption was announced by Plotina, and Dio doubted it.

list.name: Hadrian
list.note: Died at Baiae 10 Jul 138 after long illness (probably heart failure), having adopted Antoninus on condition he adopt Marcus and Lucius.

list.name: Antoninus Pius
list.note: Died at Lorium 7 Mar 161, giving the watchword 'aequanimitas'. Never left Italy as emperor.

list.name: Marcus Aurelius
list.note: Died 17 Mar 180 at Vindobona or Sirmium on campaign against the Marcomanni and Sarmatians, probably of the Antonine plague.

list.name: Lucius Verus
list.note: First formal joint Augustus with Marcus; nominal commander of the Parthian War (161-166). Died of a stroke at Altinum early 169.

list.name: Commodus
list.note: Augustus 177, sole ruler 17 Mar 180. Strangled in his bath on 31 Dec 192 by the athlete Narcissus in a plot of his mistress Marcia, chamberlain Eclectus and prefect Laetus.

list.name: Pertinax
list.note: Reigned 87 days (1 Jan to 28 Mar 193); speared by mutinous praetorians in the palace after attempting to restore discipline and finances.

list.name: Didius Julianus
list.note: Won the praetorian 'auction' with 25,000 sesterces a man (Dio 74.11); condemned by the Senate and killed in the palace 1 Jun 193 as Severus neared Rome. Reigned 66 days.

list.name: Septimius Severus
list.note: Proclaimed at Carnuntum 9 Apr 193; defeated Niger (194) and Albinus (197). Died at Eboracum 4 Feb 211 during his Caledonian war.

list.name: Caracalla
list.note: Augustus 198, sole ruler from Dec 211. Stabbed while relieving himself on the road from Edessa to Carrhae 8 Apr 217 by the guardsman Julius Martialis, at the instigation of the prefect Macrinus.

list.name: Geta
list.note: Augustus 209; killed in his mother Julia Domna's arms by centurions on Caracalla's orders, 26 Dec 211. His name was chiselled off monuments across the empire.

list.name: Macrinus
list.note: First equestrian emperor and first never to visit Rome as emperor. Defeated near Antioch 8 Jun 218 by Elagabalus' army; caught at Chalcedon/Cappadocia and executed.

list.name: Diadumenian
list.note: Son of Macrinus; Caesar 217, Augustus May 218; seized at Zeugma fleeing to Parthia and killed.

list.name: Elagabalus
list.note: Hereditary priest of the Emesene sun god; proclaimed at Raphanaea 16 May 218. Killed with his mother Julia Soaemias by the praetorians 11 or 12 Mar 222; bodies dragged and thrown in the Tiber.

list.name: Severus Alexander
list.note: Killed with his mother Julia Mamaea by mutinous troops at Vicus Britannicus (Bretzenheim) near Mogontiacum, Mar 235, ending the Severan dynasty.

list.name: Maximinus Thrax
list.note: First emperor risen from the ranks; never visited Rome. Killed with his son Maximus by soldiers of Legio II Parthica during the siege of Aquileia, spring 238.

list.name: Gordian I
list.note: Proconsul of Africa, proclaimed at Thysdrus by rebels against the procurator, aged about 80; hanged himself at Carthage on news of his son's death after about 21 days (date Jan or Mar 238 disputed).

list.name: Gordian II
list.note: Co-Augustus with his father; killed at Carthage fighting Capelianus, governor of Numidia, with Legio III Augusta.

list.name: Pupienus
list.note: Elected by a senatorial commission (vigintiviri) with Balbinus; both tortured and killed in the palace by the praetorians after about 99 days.

list.name: Balbinus
list.note: Co-emperor with Pupienus; murdered with him by the praetorians, who proclaimed the 13-year-old Gordian III.

list.name: Gordian III
list.note: Died Feb 244 on the Persian front. Shapur's ŠKZ claims he was killed in battle at Misiche (renamed Peroz-Shapur); Roman sources blame his prefect Philip; a cenotaph stood at Zaitha.

list.name: Philip the Arab
list.note: From Shahba in Trachonitis; bought peace from Shapur for 500,000 aurei; celebrated the millennium of Rome 21 Apr 248. Killed at or after the battle of Verona against Decius, c. Sep 249.

list.name: Philip II
list.note: Caesar 244, Augustus 247; killed by the praetorians in Rome on news of Verona, aged about 12.

list.name: Decius
list.note: Ordered the universal sacrifice of 250 (libelli survive from Egypt). First emperor killed by a foreign enemy, in the marsh at Abritus against Cniva's Goths, c. Jun 251.

list.name: Herennius Etruscus
list.note: Augustus May 251; killed by an arrow at Abritus shortly before or during the battle.

list.name: Hostilian
list.note: Younger son of Decius, co-Augustus with Gallus; died of the plague of Cyprian (Aurelius Victor) or was killed by Gallus (Zosimus), late 251.

list.name: Trebonianus Gallus
list.note: Governor of Moesia, proclaimed after Abritus; made peace paying the Goths. Killed with his son by their own troops at Interamna, c. Aug 253.

list.name: Volusianus
list.note: Son of Gallus, Augustus late 251; killed with his father at Interamna.

list.name: Aemilianus
list.note: Governor of Moesia proclaimed after a victory over the Goths; reigned about 88 days; killed near Spoletium by his own men as Valerian's army approached.

list.name: Valerian
list.note: Captured by Shapur I in the campaign of Edessa, spring/summer 260, the first emperor taken alive by a foreign enemy; died in captivity. Lactantius' tale that he was used as a mounting block and flayed is Christian polemic.
list.death: died in Persian captivity, date unknown

list.name: Gallienus
list.region: west 253-260; all 260-268 (minus Gallic and Palmyrene territories)
list.note: Co-Augustus 253, sole ruler 260. Killed outside Milan c. Sep 268 while besieging Aureolus, in a plot of his staff (Heraclianus, Marcianus, Cecropius; Claudius and Aurelian implicated).

list.name: Saloninus
list.note: Son of Gallienus, raised to Augustus at Colonia Agrippina while besieged by Postumus; surrendered by the garrison and killed.

list.name: Claudius II Gothicus
list.note: Won the great victory over the Goths at Naissus (269); died of plague at Sirmium Aug/Sep 270. Later claimed as ancestor of Constantine (a fiction of c. 310).

list.name: Quintillus
list.note: Brother of Claudius; reigned between 17 days and a few months at Aquileia; suicide or killed by his troops when the army chose Aurelian.

list.name: Aurelian
list.note: Reunified the empire (Palmyra 272-273, Gallic Empire 274), built the Aurelian Walls, reformed the coinage (274). Killed at Caenophrurium near Perinthus c. Sep/Oct 275 by officers duped by forged lists from his secretary Eros.

list.name: Tacitus (emperor)
list.note: Elderly general proclaimed in late 275; died at Tyana mid-276 after defeating Goths in Asia Minor, of fever (Victor) or murdered (Zosimus). His supposed descent from the historian is HA fiction.

list.name: Florianus
list.note: Tacitus' praetorian prefect and half-brother; killed by his own men near Tarsus after about 88 days when Probus' army avoided battle in the summer heat.

list.name: Probus
list.note: Restored the Rhine frontier; settled barbarians in the provinces. Killed by soldiers at Sirmium Sep/Oct 282, reportedly over forced labour draining marshes, as Carus was proclaimed.

list.name: Carus
list.note: Took Ctesiphon in 283; died near the Tigris Jul/Aug 283, officially struck by lightning; murder by the prefect Aper is suspected.

list.name: Carinus
list.note: Augustus spring 283; won at the river Margus against Diocletian (spring 285) but was killed by his own officers in or after the battle.

list.name: Numerian
list.note: Died Nov 284 near Nicomedia; the stench from his closed litter revealed the corpse. The army chose Diocletian, who killed the prefect Aper with his own hand.

list.name: Diocletian
list.note: Proclaimed at Nicomedia 20 Nov 284; created the Tetrarchy (Maximian Augustus 286; Caesars 293). Abdicated at Nicomedia 1 May 305 and retired to Spalatum; died there c. 311-312.

list.name: Maximian
list.note: Caesar 285, Augustus 1 Apr 286; abdicated with Diocletian 1 May 305, resumed the purple 306-308 with his son Maxentius, and tried again in 310 against Constantine. Forced to hang himself at Massilia 310.
list.death: forced suicide (or executed) at Massilia after his third bid for power

list.name: Constantius I
list.note: Caesar 1 Mar 293, Augustus 1 May 305; recovered Britain from Allectus (296). Died at Eboracum 25 Jul 306.

list.name: Galerius
list.note: Caesar 293 (victor over Narseh 298), Augustus 305; chief driver of the Great Persecution. Died of a gangrenous illness at Serdica c. May 311, days after his edict of toleration (30 Apr 311).

list.name: Severus II
list.note: Caesar 305, Augustus 306. His troops deserted to Maxentius; surrendered at Ravenna and was put to death (or forced to open his veins) at Tres Tabernae, 307.

list.name: Maxentius
list.note: Proclaimed at Rome 28 Oct 306 by praetorians and people; never recognized by the eastern Augusti. Drowned in the Tiber at the Milvian Bridge 28 Oct 312.

list.name: Licinius
list.note: Made Augustus at the conference of Carnuntum 11 Nov 308. Defeated by Constantine at Adrianople (3 Jul 324) and Chrysopolis (18 Sep 324); abdicated on promise of his life; hanged at Thessalonica 325.
list.death: executed at Thessalonica on a charge of plotting

list.name: Maximinus Daza
list.note: Caesar 305, Augustus 310. Routed by Licinius at Tzirallum 30 Apr 313; died at Tarsus summer 313, by poison he took (Lactantius) or illness.

list.name: Constantine I
list.note: Proclaimed at Eboracum 25 Jul 306; sole ruler after Chrysopolis (324); founded Constantinople (dedicated 11 May 330). Baptized by Eusebius of Nicomedia and died at Achyron near Nicomedia 22 May 337.

list.name: Constantine II
list.note: Augustus 9 Sep 337 after the purge of his cousins; killed in an ambush near Aquileia while invading his brother Constans' territory, early 340.

list.name: Constans
list.note: Overthrown by Magnentius at Augustodunum 18 Jan 350; caught and killed by Gaiso at Helena (Elne) at the foot of the Pyrenees.

list.name: Constantius II
list.note: Defeated Magnentius at Mursa (351) and Mons Seleucus (353). Died of fever at Mopsucrenae in Cilicia 3 Nov 361, marching against Julian, whom he named heir on his deathbed.

list.name: Julian
list.note: Proclaimed by his troops at Lutetia Feb 360; sole ruler from Nov 361; attempted pagan restoration. Wounded by a spear in a rearguard action near Maranga/Samarra 26 Jun 363 and died that night.

list.name: Jovian
list.note: Chosen by the army on Persian soil; ceded Nisibis, Singara and five Transtigritane regions to Shapur II for safe passage. Found dead at Dadastana 17 Feb 364, from charcoal fumes or bad food.

list.name: Valentinian I
list.note: Proclaimed at Nicaea 26 Feb 364; made his brother Valens eastern Augustus (28 Mar 364). Died of a stroke at Brigetio 17 Nov 375 while raging at Quadic envoys.

list.name: Valens
list.note: Admitted the Gothic Tervingi across the Danube (376). Killed at Adrianople 9 Aug 378; body never found.

list.name: Gratian
list.note: Augustus 24 Aug 367 aged 8; dropped the title pontifex maximus and removed the Altar of Victory (382). Deserted by his army near Paris to Magnus Maximus; killed at Lugdunum by Andragathius 25 Aug 383.

list.name: Valentinian II
list.note: Proclaimed aged 4 at Aquincum 22 Nov 375. Found hanged at Vienne 15 May 392 after quarrelling with his magister militum Arbogast: suicide or murder.

list.name: Theodosius I
list.note: Made Augustus at Sirmium 19 Jan 379; Nicene Christianity made the state creed (Cunctos populos 380); victor over Maximus (388) and Eugenius at the Frigidus (Sep 394). Died at Milan 17 Jan 395, the last emperor to rule both halves.

rulers.title: Western Roman emperors 395-480
rulers.note: Julius Nepos is carried to 480 because he was still the legitimate western Augustus in Constantinople's eyes after 476.

list.name: Honorius
list.note: Augustus 393 aged 8; ruled through Stilicho (executed 408). Rome sacked by Alaric 24 Aug 410. Died of oedema at Ravenna 15 Aug 423.

list.name: Constantius III
list.note: Magister militum, husband of Galla Placidia; co-Augustus 8 Feb 421, unrecognized by Constantinople; died 2 Sep 421.

list.name: Valentinian III
list.note: Installed aged 6 by an eastern army after the suppression of Joannes (23 Oct 425). Murdered Aetius with his own hand (Sep 454); killed on the Campus Martius 16 Mar 455 by Optila and Thraustila, Aetius' Hunnic retainers.

list.name: Petronius Maximus
list.note: Twice consul, prefect of Rome; proclaimed 17 Mar 455. Killed by a mob or imperial servants (stoned, by tradition) fleeing Rome 31 May 455 as Gaiseric's fleet approached; the Vandal sack followed (2-16 Jun).

list.name: Avitus
list.note: Gallo-Roman aristocrat proclaimed at Arelate with Visigothic support 9 Jul 455. Defeated near Placentia by Ricimer and Majorian 17 Oct 456 and consecrated bishop of Placentia.
list.death: died 456/457, possibly killed, on his way to Gaul

list.name: Majorian
list.note: Acclaimed 1 Apr 457 (formally 28 Dec 457). His invasion fleet was destroyed at Portus Ilicitanus near Carthago Nova (460); arrested by Ricimer at Dertona and beheaded 7 Aug 461.

list.name: Libius Severus
list.note: Ricimer's puppet, never recognized by Leo I. Died at Rome 14 Nov 465; Cassiodorus and Sidonius hint Ricimer poisoned him.

list.name: Anthemius
list.note: Eastern aristocrat sent by Leo I and proclaimed 12 Apr 467; married his daughter to Ricimer. Besieged in Rome by Ricimer and beheaded by Gundobad 11 Jul 472.

list.name: Olybrius
list.note: Husband of Placidia, daughter of Valentinian III; proclaimed by Ricimer Apr 472; died of dropsy 2 Nov 472.

list.name: Glycerius
list.note: Comes domesticorum proclaimed at Ravenna 3 Mar 473 with Gundobad's backing; deposed by Julius Nepos at Portus Jun 474 and consecrated bishop of Salona.

list.name: Julius Nepos
list.note: Magister militum of Dalmatia, nephew of Marcellinus, installed with Leo I's backing 19 Jun 474. Driven from Ravenna by Orestes 28 Aug 475; kept the title in Dalmatia, recognized by Zeno and named on some of Odoacer's coins, until murdered in his villa near Salona 9 May 480.

list.name: Romulus Augustulus
list.note: Son of the magister militum Orestes, proclaimed 31 Oct 475, never recognized by Constantinople. Deposed by Odoacer at Ravenna 4 Sep 476 and pensioned off to the Castellum Lucullanum near Naples.

rulers.title: Eastern Roman emperors 395-641 (with Constans II, crowned 641)

list.name: Arcadius
list.note: Augustus 383; ruled through Rufinus, Eutropius and Anthemius. Died 1 May 408.

list.name: Theodosius II
list.note: Augustus 402 aged 9 months. Theodosian Walls (413), University of Constantinople (425), Codex Theodosianus (438). Died 28 Jul 450 after a riding fall near the Lycus.

list.name: Marcian
list.note: Thracian officer who married Pulcheria; stopped tribute to Attila, convened the Council of Chalcedon (451). Died 27 Jan 457, leaving a large surplus.

list.name: Leo I
list.note: Thracian officer raised by Aspar; the 468 armada against the Vandals under Basiliscus cost some 64,000 lb gold and 700,000 lb silver (Lydus). Had Aspar killed (471). Died 18 Jan 474.

list.name: Leo II
list.note: Grandson of Leo I, aged about 7; crowned his father Zeno co-emperor 9 Feb 474; died Nov 474.

list.name: Zeno
list.note: Isaurian chieftain (Tarasis); driven out by Basiliscus Jan 475 to Aug 476. Henotikon (482); sent Theodoric to Italy (488). Died 9 Apr 491.

list.name: Anastasius I
list.note: Palace silentiarius chosen by Zeno's widow Ariadne. Isaurian war (492-497), copper reform (498), abolished the chrysargyron, Anastasian Wall; left 320,000 lb of gold. Died 9 Jul 518.

list.name: Justin I
list.note: Illyrian peasant who rose to command the excubitors; ended the Acacian schism (519). Died 1 Aug 527.

list.name: Justinian I
list.note: Co-emperor 1 Apr 527, sole 1 Aug 527. Corpus Iuris Civilis, Nika riot (532), Hagia Sophia (537), reconquest of Africa (533-534) and Italy (535-554), plague of 541-542. Died 14 Nov 565.

list.name: Justin II
list.note: Nephew of Justinian; refused tribute to the Avars and Persia; lost Dara (573) and went insane; Tiberius ruled as Caesar from 7 Dec 574. Died 5 Oct 578.

list.name: Tiberius II Constantine
list.note: Comes excubitorum, Caesar 574, Augustus 26 Sep 578; famously lavish. Died 14 Aug 582 (by tradition after eating bad mulberries).

list.name: Maurice
list.note: Restored Khosrow II (591) and won the Balkan wars against Avars and Slavs. Overthrown when the Danube army mutinied over wintering north of the river; made to watch five sons beheaded at Eutropius' harbour, Chalcedon, then killed 27 Nov 602.

list.name: Phocas
list.note: Centurion of the Danube army. Khosrow II's war of revenge opened in 603. Beheaded 5 Oct 610 when Heraclius' fleet reached Constantinople.

list.name: Heraclius
list.note: Son of the exarch of Africa; survived the loss of Syria, Palestine, Egypt and the siege of 626, destroyed Persian power at Nineveh (Dec 627), restored the True Cross (630), then lost Syria to the Arabs (Yarmuk 636). Died of oedema 11 Feb 641.

list.name: Constantine III
list.note: Co-emperor since 613; ruled jointly with his half-brother Heraclonas from Feb 641; died of tuberculosis 25 May 641 (rumours blamed Martina).

list.name: Heraclonas
list.note: Son of Heraclius and Martina, co-emperor 638; deposed Sep/Oct 641 after pressure from the army and Constantinopolitan crowd; nose slit and exiled with Martina to Rhodes.

list.name: Constans II
list.note: Son of Constantine III, crowned 641 aged 11. Moved his court to Syracuse (663); killed in his bath there by a chamberlain 15 Jul 668.

rulers.title: Usurpers, rebels and breakaway emperors
rulers.note: Includes a few rebels who never claimed the purple (Vindex, Gildo) where they are routinely listed with usurpers; Julian (360) and Phocas/Heraclius, who won, are listed as emperors. 'polity' marks breakaway states.

list.name: Lucius Arruntius Camillus Scribonianus
list.note: Governor of Dalmatia who called on Claudius to abdicate; his two legions (VII and XI, thereafter Claudia Pia Fidelis) deserted within five days. Killed himself or was killed on Issa.

list.name: Gaius Julius Vindex
list.note: Aquitanian senator who rose against Nero (Mar 68) and offered the throne to Galba; defeated by Verginius Rufus near Vesontio and killed himself. Did not claim the purple.

list.name: Lucius Clodius Macer
list.note: Legate of Legio III Augusta; raised Legio I Macriana liberatrix and cut Rome's grain supply; killed by the procurator Trebonius Garutianus on Galba's orders, Oct 68.

list.name: Gaius Nymphidius Sabinus
list.note: Praetorian prefect who abandoned Nero, then bid for the throne against Galba; killed by the guard in the camp, autumn 68.

list.name: Lucius Antonius Saturninus
list.note: Seized the savings of two legions at Mogontiacum (1 Jan 89); his Chattan allies were cut off by a thaw on the Rhine and he was defeated by Lappius Maximus. Domitian thereafter forbade double-legion camps.

list.name: Terentius Maximus (pseudo-Nero)
list.note: One of at least three false Neros (68/69, 79/80, 88); found support in Asia and with the Parthian Artabanus III before being surrendered.

list.name: Gaius Avidius Cassius
list.note: Victor of the Parthian War, governor of Syria with command over the East; proclaimed himself on a false report of Marcus' death (perhaps with Faustina's encouragement); killed by a centurion after about three months.

list.name: Gaius Pescennius Niger
list.note: Governor of Syria proclaimed Apr 193; beaten at Cyzicus, Nicaea and Issus (194); caught fleeing towards the Euphrates and beheaded.

list.name: Decimus Clodius Albinus
list.note: Governor of Britain; Caesar under Severus 193-195, then Augustus. Defeated at Lugdunum 19 Feb 197 in one of the largest Roman battles; killed himself or was killed, his body trampled by Severus' horse.

list.name: Gaius Petronius Magnus
list.note: Consular accused of plotting to destroy Maximinus' Rhine bridge; possibly a fabricated conspiracy (Herodian 7.1).

list.name: Titus Quartinus
list.note: Proclaimed by Osrhoenian archers loyal to Severus Alexander; murdered by their commander Macedo.

list.name: Sabinianus
list.note: Proclaimed at Carthage; crushed by the governor of Mauretania and handed over by his own followers.

list.name: Tiberius Claudius Marinus Pacatianus
list.note: Proclaimed by Danube troops in 248 (coins with ROMAE AETER AN MILL ET PRIMO); killed by his own men, which led Philip to send Decius to the Danube.

list.name: Marcus Fulvius Rufus Iotapianus
list.note: Claimed kinship with Severus Alexander; revolted against Philip's brother Priscus' exactions; killed by his own troops.

list.name: Silbannacus
list.note: Known from two antoniniani (one found 1937); context and date (perhaps 253) uncertain.

list.name: Julius Valens Licinianus
list.note: Proclaimed in Rome while Decius campaigned against the Goths; killed within days.

list.name: Titus Julius Priscus
list.note: Governor of Thrace who sided with the Goths at the fall of Philippopolis (250); declared hostis; probably died in 251.

list.name: Uranius Antoninus
list.note: Emesene priest-dynast (Sulpicius Antoninus) who repelled Shapur's attack on Emesa (253) and struck gold and silver coins; fate unknown.

list.name: Ingenuus
list.note: Governor of Pannonia proclaimed after news of Valerian's capture (or 258); defeated at Mursa by Gallienus' cavalry commander Aureolus; drowned himself or was killed.

list.name: Regalianus
list.note: Proclaimed by Ingenuus' surviving troops; coins struck at Carnuntum over Severan denarii; killed by his men or the Roxolani.

list.name: Macrianus Minor
list.note: Proclaimed with his brother Quietus after Valerian's capture, backed by their father Macrianus Major and the prefect Ballista; father and son defeated and killed in Illyricum by Aureolus, 261.

list.name: Quietus
list.note: Brother of Macrianus Minor, left in command at Emesa; killed there by the citizens with Odaenathus besieging, 261.

list.name: Lucius Mussius Aemilianus
list.note: Prefect of Egypt who backed the Macriani then claimed the purple; defeated by Gallienus' general Theodotus, strangled in prison.

list.name: Postumus
list.note: Founder of the Gallic Empire (consuls, senate and mint at Colonia/Treveri). Killed by his own troops at Mogontiacum after refusing them the sack of the city, which had backed Laelianus.

list.name: Laelianus
list.note: Rose against Postumus at Mogontiacum; defeated and killed.

list.name: Marius
list.note: Former smith (by tradition) who briefly succeeded Postumus; killed with a sword of his own making according to the HA; coinage implies a reign of some weeks.

list.name: Victorinus
list.note: Praetorian prefect of Postumus; besieged and sacked Augustodunum (270), which had appealed to Claudius II. Killed at Colonia by an officer (Attitianus) whose wife he seduced.

list.name: Domitianus II
list.note: Known from two coins (the second found at Chalgrove, Oxfordshire, 2003) and a literary mention; brief reign after Victorinus.

list.name: Tetricus I
list.note: Governor of Aquitania raised by Victoria; surrendered to Aurelian at the battle of Catalaunian Fields (Châlons) in 274, possibly by prior arrangement; walked in Aurelian's triumph and was made corrector Lucaniae.

list.name: Tetricus II
list.note: Son of Tetricus I, Caesar 273, perhaps Augustus 274; spared and later a senator.

list.name: Aureolus
list.note: Gallienus' cavalry commander; declared for Postumus, then himself, at Milan. Surrendered to Claudius II after Gallienus' murder and was killed by the soldiers.

list.name: Septimius
list.note: Proclaimed in Dalmatia during the Juthungian invasion of Italy; killed by his own troops.

list.name: Vaballathus
list.note: Son of Odaenathus; styled 'King of Kings' and corrector totius Orientis, then Augustus in 272 with his mother Zenobia as Augusta; fate after Aurelian's capture of Palmyra unknown.

list.name: Firmus
list.note: Merchant-supporter of Palmyra who allegedly held Alexandria against Aurelian (HA Firmus); possibly a corrector misrepresented as a usurper.

list.name: Bonosus
list.note: Rhine commander who rebelled after Germans burned the Rhine fleet; defeated by Probus and hanged himself ('an amphora hanging, not a man', HA).

list.name: Proculus
list.note: Rose at Lugdunum with Bonosus; betrayed by the Franks and killed.

list.name: Julius Saturninus
list.note: Moorish-born commander proclaimed in the East; killed at Apamea by Probus' troops.

list.name: Sabinus Julianus
list.note: Corrector Venetiae proclaimed on Numerian's death; defeated and killed by Carinus near Verona.

list.name: Carausius
list.note: Menapian commander of the Channel fleet; seized Britain c. 286, styled himself 'brother' of Diocletian and Maximian on coins (CARAUSIUS ET FRATRES SUI). Killed by his finance officer Allectus after losing Bononia (293).

list.name: Allectus
list.note: Carausius' rationalis and murderer; killed in battle against Constantius' prefect Asclepiodotus, who landed in fog past the British fleet off the Isle of Wight (296).

list.name: Lucius Domitius Domitianus
list.note: Proclaimed in Alexandria amid unrest over Diocletian's tax census; papyri show his regnal years; died during the revolt, succeeded by his corrector Achilleus.

list.name: Aurelius Achilleus
list.note: Led the Alexandrian resistance to Diocletian's eight-month siege; executed after the city fell (spring 298).

list.name: Eugenius
list.note: Tribune of 500 soldiers forced to dig the harbour; proclaimed, marched on Antioch, killed with his men by the citizens.

list.name: Lucius Domitius Alexander
list.note: Vicar of Africa who refused to send his son as hostage to Maxentius; cut off Rome's grain; strangled after Maxentius' prefect Rufius Volusianus took Carthage, which was sacked.

list.name: Valerius Valens
list.note: Dux limitis Daciae raised to Augustus by Licinius during the war of Cibalae; executed at Constantine's demand in the peace of Serdica (1 Mar 317).

list.name: Martinian
list.note: Licinius' magister officiorum raised to Augustus before Chrysopolis; spared at first, then put to death in Cappadocia 325.

list.name: Calocaerus
list.note: Magister pecoris camelorum who rose on Cyprus; suppressed by Constantine's half-brother Dalmatius and burned alive at Tarsus.

list.name: Magnentius
list.note: Germanic-born comes of the Ioviani and Herculiani, proclaimed at Augustodunum 18 Jan 350. Defeated at Mursa (28 Sep 351, among the bloodiest battles of the century) and Mons Seleucus (353); killed himself at Lugdunum 10 Aug 353.

list.name: Decentius
list.note: Brother or cousin of Magnentius, Caesar 351; hanged himself at Senones on news of Magnentius' death, 18 Aug 353.

list.name: Vetranio
list.note: Elderly magister peditum proclaimed at Mursa 1 Mar 350, perhaps at Constantina's prompting to block Magnentius; abdicated before the troops at Naissus 25 Dec 350 and retired to Prusa on a pension.

list.name: Julius Nepotianus
list.note: Nephew of Constantine; seized Rome with gladiators 3 Jun 350; killed after 28 days by Magnentius' officer Marcellinus, his head paraded on a lance.

list.name: Claudius Silvanus
list.note: Frankish magister peditum framed by forged letters; proclaimed at Colonia, killed after 28 days by men suborned by Ursicinus, whose staff included Ammianus (Amm. 15.5).

list.name: Procopius
list.note: Maternal relative of Julian; proclaimed at Constantinople 28 Sep 365 with Constantina's daughter displayed to the troops. Betrayed by his generals at Thyatira and Nacolia (May 366) and beheaded 27 May 366.

list.name: Marcellus
list.note: Procopius' relative and officer who claimed the purple after his execution; captured and killed by Equitius.

list.name: Firmus
list.note: Moorish prince (son of Nubel) who rebelled against the comes Romanus; his supporters may have proclaimed him; hunted down by Count Theodosius and hanged himself.

list.name: Magnus Maximus
list.note: Spanish-born commander in Britain, proclaimed 383; killed Gratian; recognized for a time by Theodosius; invaded Italy 387. Defeated at Siscia and Poetovio, executed at Aquileia 28 Aug 388. Welsh legend remembers him as Macsen Wledig.

list.name: Flavius Victor
list.note: Son of Magnus Maximus, co-Augustus; killed at Treveri by Arbogast after his father's death.

list.name: Eugenius
list.note: Rhetor made emperor by Arbogast 22 Aug 392; patron of the last pagan revival under Nicomachus Flavianus. Defeated at the Frigidus 6 Sep 394 and beheaded; Arbogast killed himself.

list.name: Gildo
list.note: Comes Africae who transferred allegiance to Arcadius and cut Rome's grain; defeated by his brother Mascezel and strangled himself or was killed at Tabraca. Did not claim the purple.

list.name: Marcus
list.note: Proclaimed by the British army in 406; killed by the troops.

list.name: Gratian (usurper)
list.note: British municipal (municeps) proclaimed after Marcus; killed after four months.

list.name: Constantine III
list.note: Soldier proclaimed in Britain for his name; crossed to Gaul after the Rhine crossing of 406 and was recognized by Honorius (409). Besieged at Arelate by Constantius, he surrendered on promise of life, was ordained, and executed before reaching Ravenna (Sep 411).

list.name: Constans (son of Constantine III)
list.note: Former monk made Caesar then Augustus by his father; killed at Vienne by Gerontius' troops 411.

list.name: Maximus of Hispania
list.note: Puppet of the general Gerontius 409-411, fled to the barbarians; re-emerged 420-422; displayed and executed at Ravenna at Honorius' tricennalia (422).

list.name: Jovinus
list.note: Gallic noble proclaimed with Burgundian and Alan support (Gundahar, Goar); made his brother Sebastianus co-emperor; captured by Athaulf's Visigoths and beheaded at Narbo by the prefect Dardanus.

list.name: Sebastianus
list.note: Brother and co-Augustus of Jovinus; killed by the Visigoths.

list.name: Priscus Attalus
list.note: Prefect of Rome made emperor by Alaric (Nov 409), deposed by him (Jul 410); raised again by Athaulf at Burdigala (414). Captured 416, paraded in Constantius' triumph, a finger cut off, exiled to Lipari.

list.name: Heraclianus
list.note: Comes Africae who executed Stilicho; consul 413; invaded Italy, was beaten at Utriculum, fled to Carthage and was beheaded there.

list.name: Joannes
list.note: Primicerius notariorum proclaimed at Rome on Honorius' death, refused recognition by Theodosius II. Betrayed at Ravenna to Aspar's army; hand cut off, paraded on an ass in the Hippodrome of Aquileia, beheaded (mid-425). Aetius arrived with 60,000 Huns three days late.

list.name: Basiliscus
list.note: Brother of Empress Verina; commander of the failed 468 Vandal expedition. Seized Constantinople Jan 475; his Encyclical alienated Chalcedonians. Surrendered to Zeno Aug 476 on promise of no bloodshed and was walled up in a dry cistern at Limnae in Cappadocia to die of starvation and exposure.

list.name: Marcianus
list.note: Son of the western emperor Anthemius and husband of Leo I's daughter Leontia; attacked the palace; ordained priest and exiled to Caesarea.

list.name: Leontius
list.note: Crowned at Tarsus by Verina at the instigation of the Isaurian general Illus; besieged at the fortress of Papyrius; beheaded with Illus 488.

list.name: Vitalian
list.note: Comes foederatorum who led a revolt of Bulgar and Hunnic foederati in the Chalcedonian cause, three times threatening Constantinople; his fleet burned in the Bosporus (515, by tradition with 'sulphur' devised by Proclus). Later consul (520), murdered in the palace in 520, Justinian suspected.

list.name: Hypatius
list.note: Nephew of Anastasius, crowned by the Nika rioters in the Hippodrome (18 Jan 532) against his will; executed the next day after Belisarius and Mundus massacred some 30,000 in the Hippodrome.

list.name: Stotzas
list.note: Leader of the great army mutiny in Byzantine Africa (from Easter 536); defeated by Belisarius and Germanus, fled to the Moors; killed at Thacia 545, mortally wounding the magister militum John.

list.name: Guntharic
list.note: Dux Numidiae who murdered the magister militum Areobindus and seized Carthage; killed at a banquet by the Armenian Artabanes after 36 days.
